deployNotes: Three pods: db (PostgreSQL), backend (FastAPI/uvicorn on 8000), and frontend (static Vite build served by nginx on 80). The Traefik proxy, Adminer and Mailcatcher from Compose are not needed, because Nexlayer handles routing and ingress.
The backend reaches the database at db.pod:5432 (POSTGRES_SERVER=db.pod, POSTGRES_PORT=5432). Never use localhost or the Compose service name 'db'.

The Compose 'prestart' service (backend/scripts/prestart.sh: wait for DB, alembic upgrade head, create initial superuser) is a one-shot job, not a daemon. Run it in the backend pod's start command before launching uvicorn, e.g. `bash scripts/prestart.sh && fastapi run --workers 4 app/main.py`.

Backend and frontend images are built from their own Dockerfiles (backend/Dockerfile uses uv; frontend/Dockerfile runs a Bun/Node build then nginx). The listed base images are the mirror.gcr.io equivalents to use in those Dockerfiles.
VITE_API_URL is baked into the frontend at build time, so set it to the backend pod's public URL before building the frontend image.
Set BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS and FRONTEND_HOST to the frontend's public URL so browser calls to the backend pass CORS and email links resolve.

Do not leave SECRET_KEY, FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD or POSTGRES_PASSWORD as 'changethis' outside local: the app refuses to start with default secrets when ENVIRONMENT is not local. The Postgres password is generated by Nexlayer and shared with the backend as POSTGRES_PASSWORD.
The exact file contents of backend/ and frontend/ were not provided, so ports and start commands follow the standard template conventions (backend 8000, frontend nginx 80).

productionPlan.summary: Three services run: a React/Vite single-page app served by nginx, a FastAPI backend on port 8000, and Postgres 18. The browser loads the frontend at / and calls the backend at /api on the same app URL. The backend reaches Postgres at db.pod:5432 and runs database migrations plus initial-user setup before it starts. What matters most for production: the Postgres data must sit on a volume, and the frontend must be built with VITE_API_URL set to the app's public URL, because that value is baked in at build time.

decisions.decision: Keep three services: frontend, backend and db. Drop adminer (a database admin UI), the Traefik proxy/traefik services and Mailcatcher. Run the one-shot prestart step (bash scripts/prestart.sh) inside the backend's start command, just before fastapi run.
decisions.why: Nexlayer routes traffic itself, so Traefik is not needed. Adminer and Mailcatcher are dev and admin helpers. prestart is a one-shot job that compose runs before backend, not a long-running service.

decisions.decision: Postgres 18 (mirror.gcr.io/library/postgres:18) in its own service, with a 5 GB volume mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data and PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata.
decisions.why: compose.yml pins postgres:18 and stores data in a named volume with that PGDATA path. Without a volume, every user and item is lost on restart.

decisions.decision: The frontend is served at / and the backend at /api on the same app URL. FRONTEND_HOST and BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS are set to the app URL. The backend reaches the database at POSTGRES_SERVER=db.pod, port 5432.
decisions.why: Every backend route, including openapi.json, is mounted under API_V1_STR=/api/v1. The CORS allow-list is BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS plus FRONTEND_HOST. nginx serves the SPA with an index.html fallback on port 80.

decisions.decision: SECRET_KEY, FIRST_SUPERUSER, FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_PASSWORD are Nexlayer keys. POSTGRES_PASSWORD uses the same ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} in the backend and the db service. ENVIRONMENT is set to production.
decisions.why: Settings reads these from the environment and builds the Postgres DSN from POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_PASSWORD/POSTGRES_SERVER. The committed .env must not supply them in production.

decisions.decision: Build both images from the repo root ('.'): backend with backend/Dockerfile (uv sync from uv.lock) and frontend with frontend/Dockerfile (Bun build, then nginx). Pass the build arg VITE_API_URL to the frontend build.
decisions.why: Both Dockerfiles copy root files (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, package.json, bun.lock) alongside their subfolder. The frontend declares ARG VITE_API_URL before bun run build.

decisions.decision: Run one backend instance with the 4 uvicorn workers that the Dockerfile CMD already uses.
decisions.why: Migrations run in the start command, so a single instance avoids parallel alembic upgrades racing each other. Four workers already give concurrency.

fix_before_production.title: Supply real secrets as Nexlayer keys, never from the committed .env
fix_before_production.why: The repo commits a .env containing SECRET_KEY, FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_PASSWORD entries. Using those values exposes the JWT signing key and admin and database passwords. Per the analysis, the app also refuses to start in production with the default values.

fix_before_production.title: Build the frontend with VITE_API_URL set to the app's public URL
fix_before_production.why: VITE_API_URL is baked into the static bundle at build time. If it is left unset or set to localhost:8000, every browser API call (login, users, items) fails.

fix_before_production.title: Switch Docker Hub base images to the mirror and build with BuildKit
fix_before_production.why: FROM python:3.10 and FROM nginx:1 pull from rate-limited Docker Hub; use mirror.gcr.io/library/python:3.10 and mirror.gcr.io/library/nginx:1 instead. The backend's RUN --mount cache and bind mounts also fail without BuildKit.

verify_after_deploy: GET / on the app URL returns 200 with the SPA's index.html
GET <app URL>/api/v1/openapi.json returns 200 JSON. This confirms /api routes reach the backend with the /api/v1 prefix intact.
Backend logs show scripts/prestart.sh completing (alembic upgrade head) before fastapi starts serving on 8000
Log in through the UI with the FIRST_SUPERUSER account and confirm the browser's calls to <app URL>/api/v1 succeed with no CORS errors
Restart the db service, then log in again and confirm previously created items still exist (the volume persisted)
open_questions: Which SMTP provider (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, EMAILS_FROM_EMAIL) should send password-recovery emails? Without one, email recovery will not work.
Do you want Sentry error reporting? If so, provide SENTRY_DSN; it is only used when ENVIRONMENT is not local.
productionPlan.nexlayer_yaml:
application:
  name: full-stack-fastapi-template
  pods:
    - name: frontend
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/full-stack-fastapi-template-frontend:planned"
      path: /
      servicePorts:
        - 80
      vars: {}
    - name: backend
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/full-stack-fastapi-template-backend:planned"
      path: /api
      servicePorts:
        - 8000
      command: "bash -c 'bash scripts/prestart.sh && exec fastapi run --workers 4 app/main.py'"
      vars:
        ENVIRONMENT: production
        PROJECT_NAME: "Full Stack FastAPI Project"
        SECRET_KEY: "${SECRET_KEY}"
        FIRST_SUPERUSER: "${FIRST_SUPERUSER}"
        FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD: "${FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD}"
        POSTGRES_SERVER: db.pod
        POSTGRES_PORT: "5432"
        POSTGRES_DB: app
        POSTGRES_USER: postgres
        POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
        FRONTEND_HOST: "<% URL %>"
        BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS: "<% URL %>"
    - name: db
      image: mirror.gcr.io/library/postgres:18
      servicePorts:
        - 5432
      vars:
        POSTGRES_DB: app
        POSTGRES_USER: postgres
        POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
        PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
      volumes:
        - name: db-data
          size: 5Gi
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
